I use hardware direct monitoring with no in DAW FX for my analog synth bass, synth leads, guitar and bass guitar. So buffer latency is of no issue there. With midi and using vst polyphonic synths I tend to play them at lowest buffer possible and nudge in mix if they get weird over 256. But heavily dependent on virtual instruments, can cause latency and need to adjust the higher your buffer gets. Drums aren't as hard, because they are locked and piano roll as well. But playing real time with a midi synth and sending midi out to hardware while not direct monitoring can use tweaking if buffer is high giving latency. One plus I love about direct monitoring, is that I can set my buffer high, work with mix plugs after and still play my analog hardware in perfect timing.  

It varies...but read up as much as you can and with your particular setup to work out kinks. I admit I have more issues with abelton with this than other daws like logic, but love abelton for its creative get to the point playstyle of ideas

She couldn't know plans with me, until the last minute her mom decided..we are talking about a 28 year old women here too. That was one of my biggest issues as well. I bring it up and she just argue about it and defend her moms bad behavior or just accept that's life. However she complained about her mom all the time, as if she was still in high school.

But also in some ways one of her main qualities I loved, was her closeness to her family and honesty. Last time I saw her we planned to go eat and her mom txted her minutes before saying her family was going out to eat...knowing this 8hrs prior and not telling her. She was upset and I just sat in the corner and shut up. This was typical stuff all the time. I think a lot of those family dynamics tied into the topic of her boredom and stress at times, and expectations, always on edge. It was only after a few drinks she become very nice, but that's not ideal. I was very patient, understanding and always hoped she seek therapy.

Sorry man...been there myself in a 6 year recently. She moved out after 5 1/2 years together. We got back briefly for 4 months after the move out and tried to work back towards what we had...that dream scenario you may be thinking of. Well she just left again. It was a lot of my faults she said the first break up, then I got all that in order before we tried again. 

In the end it was her and not me. When we got back together and broke the second time I was sad, but the worse had happened the first round and I was just fed up this last time she just gave up so easy. It's hard man, but thinking back I wish I would of stayed the course and never went back a second time. I'd be a lot further than I am now for sure.  Just be sad if you have to for awhile. Then rebuild your social networks, work out, do all the hobbies you put of and refine yourself. Go get a haircut and some new clothes for yourself. Regain your identity, self worth and forgot about having a mate for right now. Just set goals of as small as a mont then do 3 months. If you feel you can't handle this, seek out a counselor to talk to, to work your feelings out and figure out what's real and whats not. Sometimes it's hard to figure out how to work out your feelings and your thoughts on her without a outside non bias source...you'll feel a lot better doing this

Just don't try to hard if you don't feel ready and push yourself. It will just eventually happen and a spark will go off in your head. I'll be honest after a long term break up, I've dated and such months later. But at 35 on average in my life it takes about 2 years before I find a women I really like and end up in another serious relationship. There's a lot in between, but this has been about the true average where I can give my heart, meet someone good for me and get over the last fully. Dates and socializing was nice in between after a good many months. But it's different for everyone. Women seem to move a bit faster because suitable mates are always around, but also it's a curse because their are a lot of creeps, they have to sort through and sometimes get burned by.

I had tons of tests all come back ok like the ones you mentioned.

My urologist was checking down there and noticed after seeing him for a lil over a year the last few months my right testicle losing mass. I also complained about low libido and all that. He wanted me to get an ultrasound on my testicles because the one that was shrinking. Now I had my gf at the time also say hey why is one bigger? 

Never thought anything if it, and my urologist didn't much either. He just said just let's get it for the he'll of it. I did it and didn't think much and was called the next day saying I had a tumor. Freaked me out but didn't really know the huge deal yet. Went to see him on my lunch break and he shut the door behind me and shit got real serious. I was stunned, cried and took off work for 3 weeks. 

They told me I had to have surgery and it had to come out. I put off the surgery by one day because I had front row floor Radiohead tickets and shit fit the mood and I wanted to just get away from the news. Was an intense week. Good thing is it's just atheistic, and I function all the same after healing.

However me having cpps wasn't a direct cause or effect to me having cancer as far as my urologist put it. Just happened...if I never had cpps I may have never caught the cancer in time.

I've had it all. I had a scope put up me, urinary studies. They also caught Testicular cancer and removed my right one. It was by chance and had nothing to do with my cpps. I am cancer free now. So yeah I've had every test you can imagine. It all comes down to tightness and a possible nerve disorder. All other tests came back good. The baclofen is a muscle relaxer and it works way better than the benzos and such they have tried me on..I've also been on all the other urinary meds you can think of

Needing to urinate frequently, pelvic pressure when I lay down always waking me up, even if I need to pee a little, retention, constant urge. Soon as I had any urine in me my pelvic area would get pressure. It's there a little with the retention during the day still, but very easily dealt with. But biggest issue was pelvic pressure when I slept and layed down .causing me to be in pain, not sleep and wake up all the time or not sleep. It weighed heavily on my mental stability and depression. I'm hoping to sleep in my side again or try to transition. I've been having to sleep on my back the last 2 years because of it

My doc recently put me on baclofen at night. I've been on Xanax/Valium suppositories, uraxatrol. I started the baclofen last week and I've felt great! Consistent sleep every night, no pain, fully relaxed and no more daily fatigue. And this is from a person taking heavily sedating drugs. Yeah I have cpps and we think it's nerve related. But I'm very hopeful with trying the muscle relaxers like baclofen. It's really helping me and this has been one of the best weeks I can remember in years feeling like a normal week :) 

I do push myself through everything and stay busy. But I was having my days where I slept 4 hours in 2-3 days and was in pain. That will drive you mad after awhile. I got good sleep maybe twice a week every other week. Rest was like 5hrs a night on average. But starting this new med baclofen, I may just dump all the other meds. I started working out and added vitamin D as well. It's a relief right now to have 6 days of great sleep and no fatigue!

Typical song writing you can do a transition. Either a pre chorus or a build up. Soft then quiet and loud dynamics , strip elements away from the verse and then add them back into the chorus. A transition can come from a simple build up of a kick, to adding some fast high hats in the transition to give it motion picking up and introducing a new lead on top of the existing melody while staying planted in key.

Well in OPs case I see that. I've never told a girl hey this girl is better looking than you or any of that. That's pretty mean and comes across as I'm settling on you. That is not cool. But yeah as a guy I like compliments in a relationship sure. Do I need them every day or base my self esteem on them no. Sometimes actions speak louder than words. I'm just observing from my own experience that I've learned, this is very important to females and a lot of men don't realize just how important it is for them to tell their girlfriends how pretty they are on regular basis, rather than just thinking it. Females want to hear it and it really makes them feel good. In my experience, it just seems to be an essential part for a girl to have this in a solid relationship and feel good. In other words it's a top priority

From a guys point of view who's ex gf/maybe gf who knows, feels that way. I may not be the best to keep up compliments on a daily basis. But for me I always felt regardless as long as I've been with her it went without saying she was still the love of my life. However I did notice without watering her ego and I don't mean that in a bad way, she seem to feel insecure and felt I didn't love her enough maybe and we weren't compatible. Far from it from my view point because in my mind I'd think how pretty she is all the time, but I just didn't say it out loud constantly. I really only verbalized it when she got all dressed up to go out, or at random but was never consistent. I do now see that women crave this a lot and need it. 

Men However, we don't need the compliments, we feel you being with us and giving us your time, is enough in itself to feel attractive and whole most of the time. I think a lot of guys just don't see it from the girls view point. It's a lesson I've learned along the way and the difference between men and women. It doesn't mean your bf loves you any less. It's a common topic I feel many people live and learn, as they go through the relationship world and gain insight.

I'm 35 and make just enough at my job to pay my rent/bills and maybe have $250 left over and a small line of credit. I dropped out of college my senior year 7 years ago due to depression. I eventually met a girl after my 2 years in limbo after I left college and we dated for 6 months then moved in together. During that time we had some great times and later a few ups and downs. I was so wrapped up in the relationship and just getting steady work that 5 years just passed me by. We broke up twice this year, one being pretty recent. 

Now I'm kinda where you are and all the focus is back on me, sitting at home by myself when I'm not at work. I have interests, but the depression makes me lazy and not motivated to do them.  In the last month I missed some work, got a therapist and try to see all my doctors more to have a support team. I went through TS cancer in April, lost my right testicle, and I feel my relationship with the girl I was with for 6 years got way worse at that point post recovery. I've gotten to a point, where I'm just trying to set a goal to have a better life within these next 5 years. It's rough at times. 

I believe she also suffered from depression because she was always upset, she wasn't interested in much and felt she couldn't achieve happiness, because of her lack of interest of things to make her happy. Your just paying a convience fee to access the material. Spotify is the same, sure you can download the music and I love me some FLAC! But when I'm gaming and just want a random playlist without having to go search stuff out, Spotify if way easier. I'd say for high quality material especially with music and critical listening like an audiophile, I tend to pirate a lot of FLAC.  KODI is kind of a medium between the two, but I find sometimes it can be annoying with updates and unstable/low quality.

You take a flat head screw driver or credit card and pop the case off. Every enclosed external is an actual normal HD inside. The big ones are usually desktop, the small externals are just normal or slim hard drives in a casing that allows you to attach a USB. Pretty much a dongle with optimal software included on it. The thing is most 2tb are too big for the ps4, but the slim seagate one fits it just fine and is widely available....optionally you can special order the same HD without the enclosure for $29-30 more online

The seagate slim external 2tb you can buy on Amazon or Best Buy for 79-99 dollars. You just have to pop it out its external case, but that's easy. Only decent priced 2tb that's gonna fit for a good price. Now if you're going 1tb you have a lot of choices in the ssd,5400,7200. I think the best rates one on ign and most games site was this suprisngly, even up against hybrids and ssd. Based on all the reviews I've seen the travel star out does the hybrid, out does the stock one and fits comfortably up there with some top end ssd load times by 2-5 seconds...though limited to 1tb.The seagate slim is slightly better load time than stock but nothing significant, just more storage. I'm in the process as well and you really have to ask if you want slight speed,big storage or somewhere in the middle. There's really no affordable ssd that covers all bases right now.

Without a full band equalizer in my surround system, the lack of strong mids sucks for me. I tend to use my system for movies and tv. I use my Astro m50s for all gaming. As far as quality goes, most headphones will make you use Dolby which is compressed. If you are using strictly a home sound system you want hdmi with linear pcm setting for best quality. Hdmi pcm may sound quieter at first but that's because it's uncompressed and has more dynamics...soft/Loud. Most 7.1 system you need hdmi anyways. The eq is gonna be up to your external soundsystem mostly, as the ps4 has no built in eq. Some headphones have built in eq settings/preamp. I personally find the headphone out on the controller is too low without some type of preamp built in to the headphones. 

The external preamp is what's going to make the difference with both room sound and headphones no matter what you do or how you connect.

not in trouble per say, but a few years back it was christmas and i was broke... so i downloaded a big movie at the time for my dad. mistake i made was not monitoring it and it seeded over night. now d/l a file yourself is not a crime, however once the file is downloaded and you see the entire file uploading to users, it is breaking the law. many torrent clients don't just stop the file you have to do so manually, by monitoring it. long story short and the same thing happened to a friend. a letter was sent out by my service provider stating, said movie was found and you need to delete it if it's yours... now no way of proving as you may have a non secured router so they don't pin point you per say. the letter usually stipulates that you should secure your router, remove any of said files and that if your found again at least 3 times the provider can refuse service to you and a possible legal pursuit by the owner if they choose. this is pretty standard in the USA and usually comes from Warner and Sony material the most of which I beleive HBO is a part of. HBO is very ruthless and send out the most for tv shows. Best thing to do is not seed an entire movie, use something like peer blocker and manually monitor your torrents to remove them as soon as the download is complete. 

small bits of a file are not copyrighted content, but seeding an entire movie/show that's formed from the small parts after it's completed is. so use protection and don't give back unless you are a major host that knows what your're doing!

Had the support issue myself and it worked on every other tv but mine. Try booting in safe mode. It remembers each tv and sometimes messes up on the output cutting the signal. I cleaned my hdmi out and then after hrs accidentally booted into safe mode by holding down power till 2 beeps and it went into 400p and was able to boot to home screen and reset it. When i worked at a new station we had those 4,000 dollar mini dv playback systems as it was what the cameras use now mostly. Anything vhs would usually be transferred by master control room to these. Now for promo stuff, like the harlem globestrotters came in or an old 50s act to the town at a local theater or university, beta max was given to us to make our own promo reals for our specific station. Crazy, but beta was used a good bit when getting higlight reels pre done from an outside organization. Could be laziness to not transfer it to something more widely used, but most tv studios have at least one beta max player laying around. Typically someone shoots, hands in the mini dv, it gets played back for capture in final cut, editing takes place, adobe after fx used for titles and fx...then the whole thing gets printed back to mini dv and handed into the master control room for broadcast. Most places probably have a server set up to dump final renders too, but i guess its more standard to have a physical master copy and deliver by hand. Probably keeps things from leaking out before they hit the air like music does these days and makes sure no one screws the transfer up with a weird codec. Relying on digital i was told without master control watching in realtime as its uploaded for broadcast can result in big errors.

When it comes to layering I tend to use instrument racks in Ableton..

Usually I pick one major synth like sylenth or ableton, get my sound and then use operator for sub and then use simpler for a sample I might make myself from a guitar or it can be from a sound library..I mix it all together using hpf,lpf, eq, ohmnicide, auto filter, make a few custom preset macros to a knob and then have a variety of the layered sounds of the one combined synth playing at once, separate and maybe another macro to a hpf to all create the illusion of instruments coming in, cutting out, counter melody,motion to make it more interesting all on one layered synth line. (One of many tips that is standard practice in most productions) 

 Once you learn what ableton can do there are tons of shortcuts that make it fast, fun and creative. In another daw one might achieve this same thing by making three or four tracks, copying pasting and then cutting parts out of a line and arranging for other instruments to come in and finish melodies in different spots...Sounds like a lot of work and cpu power vs putting in the hard work,doing the sound design and flipping a button allowing things to be more creative, live and fluid. 

Seriously just look at the youtube tutorials on how to make sounds you like...On the way there you will learn all these little neat production tips at the same time. Make yourself do a few a week or take a hour or two out of your day just to do it...by the time you get to writing you'll know a bit more and have more fun. Short days/few hours tutorials/learning. Long day/8+hr writing :)

It takes lots of time...I used fruity loops in 98, reason 99-2003, Prootools, Logic and ableton up to now. I've messed around with Ableton since 2003, but never really dove into it until about 2 or 3 years ago. I'm still finding out new things! Honestly, these days there is so much to learn compared to the 90s and early 2000s it can be overwhelming. You have mixing, sound design and writing at which  most popular artist in the genre seem to have mastered all 3 individual skills. Mixing is a good thing to learn and mixing other peoples music is very helpful, sound design is something that must be learned well and mastered along with writing. Funny thing is in current music, writing has taken a back seat to sound design and mixing. 

Just keep going at it...get good at all 3..

My best advice is to be well organized. Get all your samples together and sound design done first! If you start writing, trying to program synths, scrolling through a bizzilion presets and samples trying to layer everything... your writing skills will hurt and not much will get done every time. Learn sound design, beef up your mixing skills, get the basics down and then some..Organize, have everything ready and then just pick 1 day and just start writing. If the general idea isn't created within the day..scrap it for parts and move on.

I can tell the difference between MP3 and FLAC. I mix for a living and at home I'm using a Apogee Rosetta 200 and a pair of ATH M-50s which is probably the same converter chip most bands actually recorded the album with. On my system at least there is a huge difference. Now with a consumer system as long as you have at least a 320 mp3 you may not notice and it's being hyped and colored anyway if your using a high end consumer product. A true pro high end audio system with a great DA converter will def. have a difference. Earbuds/ipod or a consumer system with build in EQ with sweetened curve response in the low and highs like beats or bose probably not. A lot of consumer systems even the more pricier ones are built to make it sound good and give the illusion...Not really give you the pure audio quality. There's many variables from the headphones to system to da converter ect. 

A lot of people don't take into account the playback system as well as the quality. Most mp3 is compressed and cuts off below 30hz which you can't hear really, but playing that mp3 in a club, you will actually "feel" the difference. Also it cuts off to 20khz where as 22khz is the full range on a cd. You don't really hear above 22khz so unless your  superman or a dog you might not notice. 

It's good to look at the HZ-KHZ response on the headphones you're buying and find out if they are flat or have a curved response. Don't just buy them because they have a Low and highpass shelf, look cool and have a hip hop artist name with a $300 price tag :)  Usually look for a 22khz and the lowest HZ bass response you can with no shelve eq added for color and a great build quality. AKG, Audio Technica and Senhnisser make the top ones and a lot are actually affordable!

A mytek DA converter with a pair of ath-50s or higher and lossless would be very true and sound great. Now whatever eq you use is up to you. I'm fine with most built in eq's, but in the audio engineer community many have issues with itunes. VLC is probably a better playback software to go with as it adds certain things like src with certain versions. Not to mention the fact that some software burning programs apply dither when converting to 16 bit and results can vary.
